The belly sags, the hair turns white, the row of teeth weakens.
The chest bends, the back curves, and the lips droop.
Hanging on a stick with one hand, the young women mock and laugh.
They say, 'This old man is a frail fellow', and he coughs.
With a rattling cough, the eyes are dim and the voice falters.
Blind and deaf, he cannot hear or see anything.
Diseases come, and they settle in the body.
Though he has learned talk, the body suffers from the illness.
The wealth and children he held are now debts, and he is in pain.
His wife weeps and cries, and the messengers of death arrive.
Standing, the body releases its impurities, and the life ebbs away.
Quickly, at dusk, come on your peacock, O Lord.
Father, come, O king Raganayaka, come.
Come, my child, come, my son.
Come to my eyes, come, my dear life, beautiful one.
Come here, O king, come and take me in your arms.
Come and eat, come and wear the flowers.
Thus said Kosalai (the mother) with love, the son of Mayon (Vishnu).
O Murugan who delights the heart, the child of the Kurava woman.
O beauty of Valli, the one who freed the gods from prison.
O destroyer of the demons who fell with their clan.
The one who wears the moon and the river on his head is Lord Shiva.
O son of Shiva, the waves break upon the shore.
You who live happily in Tiruchendur, the great Lord.
